ImageDescription.value:
Elizabeth I coat of arms, Gorey Castle. Placed above the Fourth Gate in 1593.
The shield, supported by the crowned lion of England and the dragon of Wales, is divided into quarters.
The three leopards of England are shown in the first and fourth quarters.
The second and third quarters show the fleur de lys of France.

Above is the motto "Dieu et mon droit" (God and my right).

ImageDescription.value:
Charles II coat of arms, Gorey Castle. King Charles had his coat of arms placed in a prominent position on the castle after the restoration of the Monarchy in 1660.
The terrified crowned lion of England and the unicorn of Scotland support the shield.
The shield is divided into quarters with the first and fourth quarters bearing Henry IV's shield.
Scotland's lion rampant is shown in the second quarter and the Irish harp is in the third quarter.

The garter bears the motto "Honi soit qui mal y pense" (Shamed be he who thinks ill of it).
